1| # yellowbrick.cluster.elbow
2| # Implements the elbow method for determining the optimal number of clusters.
3| #
4| # Author:   Benjamin Bengfort <bbengfort@districtdatalabs.com>
5| # Created:  Thu Mar 23 22:36:31 2017 -0400
6| #
7| # Copyright (C) 2016 District Data Labs
8| # For license information, see LICENSE.txt
9| #
10| # ID: elbow.py [5a370c8] benjamin@bengfort.com $
11| 
12| """
13| Implements the elbow method for determining the optimal number of clusters.
14| https://bl.ocks.org/rpgove/0060ff3b656618e9136b
15| """
16| 
17| ##########################################################################
18| ## Imports
19| ##########################################################################
20| 
21| import time
22| 
23| from .base import ClusteringScoreVisualizer
24| from ..exceptions import YellowbrickValueError
25| 
26| from sklearn.metrics import silhouette_score
27| from sklearn.metrics import calinski_harabaz_score
28| from sklearn.metrics.pairwise import pairwise_distances
29| from sklearn.preprocessing import LabelEncoder
30| 
31| 
32| ## Packages for export
33| __all__ = [
34|     "KElbowVisualizer", "distortion_score"
35| ]
36| 
37| 
38| ##########################################################################
39| ## Metrics
40| ##########################################################################
41| 
42| def distortion_score(X, labels, metric='euclidean'):
43|     """
44|     Compute the mean distortion of all samples.
45| 
46|     The distortion is computed as the the sum of the squared distances between
47|     each observation and its closest centroid. Logically, this is the metric
48|     that K-Means attempts to minimize as it is fitting the model.
49| 
50|     .. seealso:: http://kldavenport.com/the-cost-function-of-k-means/
51| 
52|     Parameters
53|     ----------
54|     X : array, shape = [n_samples, n_features] or [n_samples_a, n_samples_a]
55|         Array of pairwise distances between samples if metric == "precomputed"
56|         or a feature array for computing distances against the labels.
57| 
58|     labels : array, shape = [n_samples]
59|         Predicted labels for each sample
60| 
61|     metric : string
62|         The metric to use when calculating distance between instances in a
63|         feature array. If metric is a string, it must be one of the options
64|         allowed by `sklearn.metrics.pairwise.pairwise_distances
65|         <http://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.metrics.pairwise.pairwise_distances.html#sklearn.metrics.pairwise.pairwise_distances>`_
66| 
67|     .. todo:: add sample_size and random_state kwds similar to silhouette_score
68|     """
69|     # Encode labels to get unique centers and groups
70|     le = LabelEncoder()
71|     labels = le.fit_transform(labels)
72|     unique_labels = le.classes_
73| 
74|     # Sum of the distortions
75|     distortion = 0
76| 
77|     # Loop through each label (center) to compute the centroid
78|     for current_label in unique_labels:
79|         # Mask the instances that belong to the current label
80|         mask = labels == current_label
81|         instances = X[mask]
82| 
83|         # Compute the center of these instances
84|         center = instances.mean(axis=0)
85| 
86|         # Compute the square distances from the instances to the center
87|         distances = pairwise_distances(instances, [center], metric=metric)
88|         distances = distances ** 2
89| 
90|         # Add the mean square distance to the distortion
91|         distortion += distances.mean()
92| 
93|     return distortion
94| 
95| 
96| ##########################################################################
97| ## Elbow Method
98| ##########################################################################
99| 
100| KELBOW_SCOREMAP = {
101|     "distortion": distortion_score,
102|     "silhouette": silhouette_score,
103|     "calinski_harabaz": calinski_harabaz_score,
104| }
105| 
106| 
107| class KElbowVisualizer(ClusteringScoreVisualizer):
108|     """
109|     The K-Elbow Visualizer implements the "elbow" method of selecting the
110|     optimal number of clusters for K-means clustering. K-means is a simple
111|     unsupervised machine learning algorithm that groups data into a specified
112|     number (k) of clusters. Because the user must specify in advance what k to
113|     choose, the algorithm is somewhat naive -- it assigns all members to k
114|     clusters even if that is not the right k for the dataset.
115| 
116|     The elbow method runs k-means clustering on the dataset for a range of
117|     values for k (say from 1-10) and then for each value of k computes an
118|     average score for all clusters. By default, the ``distortion_score`` is
119|     computed, the sum of square distances from each point to its assigned
120|     center. Other metrics can also be used such as the ``silhouette_score``,
121|     the mean silhouette  coefficient for all samples or the
122|     ``calinski_harabaz_score``, which computes the ratio of dispersion between
123|     and within clusters.
124| 
125|     When these overall metrics for each model are plotted, it is possible to
126|     visually determine the best value for K. If the line chart looks like an
127|     arm, then the "elbow" (the point of inflection on the curve) is the best
128|     value of k. The "arm" can be either up or down, but if there is a strong
129|     inflection point, it is a good indication that the underlying model fits
130|     best at that point.
131| 
132|     Parameters
133|     ----------
134| 
135|     model : a Scikit-Learn clusterer
136|         Should be an instance of a clusterer, specifically ``KMeans`` or
137|         ``MiniBatchKMeans``. If it is not a clusterer, an exception is raised.
138| 
139|     ax : matplotlib Axes, default: None
140|         The axes to plot the figure on. If None is passed in the current axes
141|         will be used (or generated if required).
142| 
143|     k : integer or tuple
144|         The range of k to compute silhouette scores for. If a single integer
145|         is specified, then will compute the range (2,k) otherwise the
146|         specified range in the tuple is used.
147| 
148|     metric : string, default: ``"distortion"``
149|         Select the scoring metric to evaluate the clusters. The default is the
150|         mean distortion, defined by the sum of squared distances between each
151|         observation and its closest centroid. Other metrics include:
152| 
153|         - **distortion**: mean sum of squared distances to centers
154|         - **silhouette**: mean ratio of intra-cluster and nearest-cluster distance
155|         - **calinski_harabaz**: ratio of within to between cluster dispersion
156| 
157|     timings : bool, default: True
158|         Display the fitting time per k to evaluate the amount of time required
159|         to train the clustering model.
160| 
161|     kwargs : dict
162|         Keyword arguments that are passed to the base class and may influence
163|         the visualization as defined in other Visualizers.
164| 
165|     Examples
166|     --------
167| 
168|     >>> from yellowbrick.cluster import KElbowVisualizer
169|     >>> from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
170|     >>> model = KElbowVisualizer(KMeans(), k=10)
171|     >>> model.fit(X)
172|     >>> model.poof()
173| 
174|     Notes
175|     -----
176| 
177|     If you get a visualizer that doesn't have an elbow or inflection point,
178|     then this method may not be working. The elbow method does not work well
179|     if the data is not very clustered; in this case you might see a smooth
180|     curve and the value of k is unclear. Other scoring methods such as BIC or
181|     SSE also can be used to explore if clustering is a correct choice.
182| 
183|     For a discussion on the Elbow method, read more at
184|     `Robert Gove's Block <https://bl.ocks.org/rpgove/0060ff3b656618e9136b>`_.
185| 
186|     .. todo:: add parallelization option for performance
187|     .. todo:: add different metrics for scores and silhoutte
188|     .. todo:: add timing information about how long its taking
189|     """
190| 
191|     def __init__(self, model, ax=None, k=10,
192|                  metric="distortion", timings=True, **kwargs):
193|         super(KElbowVisualizer, self).__init__(model, ax=ax, **kwargs)
194| 
195|         # Get the scoring method
196|         if metric not in KELBOW_SCOREMAP:
197|             raise YellowbrickValueError(
198|                 "'{}' is not a defined metric "
199|                 "use one of distortion, silhouette, or calinski_harabaz"
200|             )
201| 
202|         # Store the arguments
203|         self.scoring_metric = KELBOW_SCOREMAP[metric]
204|         self.timings = timings
205| 
206|         # Convert K into a tuple argument if an integer
207|         if isinstance(k, int):
208|             k = (2, k+1)
209| 
210|         # Expand k in to the values we will use, capturing exceptions
211|         try:
212|             k = tuple(k)
213|             self.k_values_ = list(range(*k))
214|         except:
215|             raise YellowbrickValueError((
216|                 "Specify a range or maximal K value, the value '{}' "
217|                 "is not a valid argument for K.".format(k)
218|             ))
219| 
220| 
221|         # Holds the values of the silhoutte scores
222|         self.k_scores_ = None
223| 
224|     def fit(self, X, y=None, **kwargs):
225|         """
226|         Fits n KMeans models where n is the length of ``self.k_values_``,
227|         storing the silhoutte scores in the ``self.k_scores_`` attribute.
228|         This method finishes up by calling draw to create the plot.
229|         """
230| 
231|         self.k_scores_ = []
232|         self.k_timers_ = []
233| 
234|         for k in self.k_values_:
235|             # Compute the start time for each  model
236|             start = time.time()
237| 
238|             # Set the k value and fit the model
239|             self.estimator.set_params(n_clusters=k)
240|             self.estimator.fit(X)
241| 
242|             # Append the time and score to our plottable metrics
243|             self.k_timers_.append(time.time() - start)
244|             self.k_scores_.append(
245|                 self.scoring_metric(X, self.estimator.labels_)
246|             )
247| 
248|         self.draw()
249| 
250|         return self
251| 
252|     def draw(self):
253|         """
254|         Draw the elbow curve for the specified scores and values of K.
255|         """
256|         # Plot the silhouette score against k
257|         self.ax.plot(self.k_values_, self.k_scores_, marker="D", label="score")
258| 
259|         # If we're going to plot the timings, create a twinx axis
260|         if self.timings:
261|             self.axes = [self.ax, self.ax.twinx()]
262|             self.axes[1].plot(
263|                 self.k_values_, self.k_timers_, label="fit time",
264|                 c='g', marker="o", linestyle="--", alpha=0.75,
265|             )
266| 
267|         return self.ax
268| 
269|     def finalize(self):
270|         """
271|         Prepare the figure for rendering by setting the title as well as the
272|         X and Y axis labels and adding the legend.
273|         """
274|         # Get the metric name
275|         metric = self.scoring_metric.__name__.replace("_", " ").title()
276| 
277|         # Set the title
278|         self.set_title(
279|             '{} Elbow for {} Clustering'.format(metric, self.name)
280|         )
281| 
282|         # Set the x and y labels
283|         self.ax.set_xlabel('k')
284|         self.ax.set_ylabel(metric.lower())
285| 
286|         # Set the second y axis labels
287|         if self.timings:
288|             self.axes[1].grid(False)
289|             self.axes[1].set_ylabel("fit time (seconds)", color='g')
290|             self.axes[1].tick_params('y', colors='g')
